title: Jesus, We Bow Before Thy Feet
description: Jesus, We Bow Before Thy Feet in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book III, prepared for the Lord's Supper, hymn 18, headed “The same”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Long Metre (8.8.8.8). This page sets the words to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Je-sus, we bow be-fore thy feet, Thy ta-ble is di-vine-ly stor'd: Thy sa-cred flesh our souls have eat, 'Tis liv-ing bread; we thank thee, Lord!

lines: Jesus, we bow before thy feet,
Thy table is divinely stor'd:
Thy sacred flesh our souls have eat,
'Tis living bread; we thank thee, Lord!
And here we drink our Saviour's blood,
We thank thee, Lord, 'tis generous wine;
Mingled with love the fountain flow'd
From that dear bleeding heart of thine.
On earth is no such sweetness found,
For the Lamb's flesh is heavenly food;
In vain we search the globe around
For bread so fine, or wine so good.
Carnal provisions can at best
But cheer the heart, or warm the head,
But the rich cordial that we taste
Gives life eternal to the dead.
Joy to the Master of the feast,
His name our souls for ever bless:
To God the King, and God the Priest,
A loud Hosanna round the place.

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
